proof:
The inequalities are affine and all side lengths are positive. Every real fiber box is the coordinatewise Minkowski interpolation of the endpoint boxes, proving the hull equality. The volumes at $-1,0,1$ are $w_-=A(2+B)^{d-1}$, $w_0=(1+A)(1+B)^{d-1}$ and $w_+=(2+A)B^{d-1}$. The identities $A/(2+A)=s^{d-1}$ and $B/(2+B)=s$ give $w_-=w_+$. The fiber centers depend affinely on $z$, so the mixed centroid is $(0,(1+A)/2,(1+B)/2,\ldots,(1+B)/2)$.

With $t=1-z+B$, integrating the section volume yields
$$
V_s=\frac{2+A+B}{d}\big((2+B)^d-B^d\big)
-\frac{(2+B)^{d+1}-B^{d+1}}{d+1}.
$$
As $s\downarrow0$, $M_s=w_0+2w_-\to1$ and this expression tends to $2^{d+1}/[d(d+1)]$. For any prescribed upper bound choose a finite $d$ with larger limit and then choose a sufficiently small positive rational $s$.

statement: For $d\ge2$ and $0<s<1$ put $A=2s^{d-1}/(1-s^{d-1})$, $B=2s/(1-s)$. Let $C_s\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be given by $-1\le z\le1$, $0\le x_1\le1+z+A$, and $0\le x_i\le1-z+B$ for $2\le i\le d$. It is the convex hull of its mixed intersection, has exactly three positive integer fibers and its actual mixed centroid lies at the center of its central fiber. If $V_s$ and $M_s$ are the ambient and mixed volumes, then $\lim_{s\downarrow0}V_s/M_s=2^{d+1}/[d(d+1)]$. Thus the ratio is unbounded over $d$, even for rational $s$.
title: Unbounded ambient to mixed volume at an integer-base centroid
